title: Reduction Operations and Characterizations of $S^1$-Flows in Graphs
summary: Thomassen (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 108 (2014), 81-91) showed that every graph admitting a nowhere-zero $3$-flow also admits an $S^1$-flow. He also proved that the converse holds for cubic graphs, but constructed counterexamples showing it fails in general. Wang et al. (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 29 (2015), 2166-2178) presented a couple of sufficient conditions under which the existence of an $S^1$-flow guarantees the existence of a nowhere-zero 3-flow.
